## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Normalize keys in `Cache.set` so callers can retrieve entries written with mixed-case keys.

## Changes

The pull request adds `Cache.set`, raises the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds, and adds tests for round trips, the default TTL constant, and expiry.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Normalize keys before storing entries — After `set("Alpha", 1)`, both `get("Alpha")` and `get("alpha")` return `None`. The setter stores the original key, while `get` lowercases it before looking it up. — Callers who write a mixed-case key lose access to the cached value. — Fix: Store entries under `key.lower()` and extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip`.

## Suggestions

- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Expire entries at their deadline — With a one-second TTL, an entry set at monotonic time `1000.0` still returns its value at `1001.0`. The setter records that deadline, and `get` uses a strict `<` comparison at `app/cache.py:21`. — A lookup at the exact expiry timestamp can return a value whose configured lifetime has elapsed. — Fix: Use `expires <= time.monotonic()` at `app/cache.py:21` and extend `test_entries_expire`.
